title: Oat and honey bath soak
subtitle: A soothing dry blend for sensitive and dry skin
excerpt: A dry bath-soak blend of colloidal oats, honey powder, sea salt, and lavender essential oil. Scoop a portion under the running tap to dissolve. Soothes dry, itchy, or wind-chapped skin. Makes enough for 8 baths.
sourceNotes: Oatmeal in dermatology: Kurtz, E. S. and Wallo, W., 'Colloidal oatmeal: history, chemistry and clinical properties', Journal of Drugs in Dermatology (2007, open access). Sea salt in bath preparations: general spa formulation reference.

recipe.yieldDescription: ~400 g dry blend (8 baths at 50 g per bath)
recipe.batchNotes: Make 800 g at a time and store in a large jar.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Mix and store in a sealed jar; stable for six months.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Keeps six months in a sealed jar in a dry bathroom cupboard. The lavender scent fades over time; the soothing properties of the oats and sea salt remain. Discard if the blend clumps, smells off, or shows any sign of moisture damage.

glossaryTerms.definition: Oats ground to a fine powder that disperses evenly in water rather than sinking to the bottom. Colloidal oats form a protective, soothing film on the skin surface and are one of the few over-the-counter ingredients with FDA-recognised skin-protective properties.

content.text: This is a dry soak blend of oat flour, sea salt, and lavender essential oil for the bath. The oat flour acts as
in warm water, forming a soft, milky layer that soothes dry or itchy skin. The sea salt gently mineralises. Scoop under the running tap so the powder disperses before you step in.

items.prepNote: finely ground oat flour (not rolled oats); disperses to a milky suspension in the bath
spa-grade coarse sea salt; dissolves in the bath

content.text: Combine the oat flour and sea salt in a bowl. Add the bicarbonate of soda if using.
Stir in the lavender essential oil drop by drop, mixing as you go so it distributes evenly.

Run the bath to a comfortable temperature. Scoop 50 g of the blend (about 3 tablespoons) into the running water. Stir the water briefly to help the oat flour disperse. The bath water should turn slightly milky. Soak for 15 to 20 minutes. Pat the skin dry rather than rubbing, which removes the protective oat film.
Keeps six months in a sealed jar in a dry cupboard. Use a dry spoon to scoop; moisture causes the oat flour to clump. Discard if the blend smells off or shows moisture damage.
